our_argument_summary: WIN-001 is Refuted by Data. The 11.78 Hz value traces to Tesla's 1905 apparatus-coherence parameter from US Patent 787412, not a measurement of Earth's resonance. The dome's two derivations (f=c/(2*disc_thickness) on wins.html and f=v_a/(2*r_disc) on live-power) algebraically collapse to the same Earth-sphere arithmetic because v_a=1.574c was fit to absorb the residual between disc_thickness=12,717 km and Earth diameter 12,742 km. The new c-vs-v_a cross-WIN paragraph adds a structural argument: applying v_a consistently to WIN-029 inflates its claimed firmament-height match from 5.3% to 66% error; applying c consistently to WIN-001 with r_disc gives 7.49 Hz, not 11.78 Hz. Both WINs survive only by per-WIN speed selection on a circuit the dome explicitly calls singular (r=0.999 cross-correlation).

holes_found.description: New "Same circuit, two incompatible wave speeds" paragraph asserts the dome publishes "no dispersion relation omega(k), no mode index, and no cavity eigenvalue calculation that would justify the per-WIN speed selection." I verified this is currently true by greping all 9 raw-text/ files for those terms — zero hits. The hole: this is a moving-target claim. If the dome author adds a single dispersion paragraph to model.html in response to this critique, the entire dispersion-law preempt collapses without our text being touched. Recommend a defensive footnote: "(verified absent in dome corpus as of 2026-06-20 site snapshot — any subsequent dispersion-relation publication should restate this passage to address it specifically rather than rest on its absence)".
holes_found.recommendation: Add a one-sentence verification-stamp footnote anchoring the absence-claim to a specific dome-corpus snapshot date so reactive insertions can be detected. Alternative: convert the preempt from "the dome publishes no X" to "any proposed dispersion relation must also explain why H_0 appears as 8537 km in the same-circuit framing on live-power line 147 but 9086 km in WIN-029's match calculation" — that frames it as an unmet burden rather than a current-state assertion.

holes_found.description: The new paragraph quotes the cross-correlation "r = 0.999 between Tesla's frequency and the Schumann fundamental." This is verified at raw-text/08-live-power.txt:147 — citation is sourced. But the paragraph does not flag the obvious mathematical degeneracy: a Pearson r between exactly two values (11.79 Hz, 7.83 Hz) and (7.83 Hz, 7.83 Hz) is either undefined or trivially 1.0; the "0.999" figure can only be meaningful if it is a time-series correlation over many samples. The dome publishes neither the sample size n nor the time-window. A determined defender will not raise this (it weakens his framing), but the missing critique leaves a sharp visual finding on the table.
holes_found.recommendation: Append after the existing r=0.999 quote: "(the dome publishes neither sample size n nor the time window producing this correlation; with only two scalar frequencies in play, r=0.999 either describes a degenerate two-point fit or an unreported timeseries — neither is a substantive correlation claim)."

holes_found.description: The new secondary-source aggregation citation honestly flags teslauniverse.com as not-a-primary-source. This is correct epistemic practice, but creates an asymmetric vulnerability: a fair-minded dome defender can now say "You concede your own attribution for the 6/18/30 Hz figures rests on a secondary aggregator. Why should the reader treat your refutation of the dome's prediction as authoritative when both sides are arguing from secondary?" The current text does not preempt this — it just discloses the weakness. Either tighten the attribution (locate the actual Colorado Springs Notes page numbers, available as the published 1978 transcript) or acknowledge the limitation does not affect the larger argument.
holes_found.recommendation: Append: "(the 6/18/30 Hz values appear in the published transcript of the Colorado Springs Notes, ed. Aleksandar Marincic, Nolit 1978, pp 333-336; teslauniverse.com is cited only as a convenience locator). The exact figures do not affect the larger argument: even Tesla's best-case Earth-resonance speculation misses the Schumann band by 25-44% per mode." Or, if primary verification is not in scope, change "secondary-source aggregation" to "convenience locator for the published Colorado Springs Notes (Marincic 1978)" — that frames it as a citation shortcut rather than a sourcing concession.

holes_found.description: The c-vs-v_a swap arithmetic claims v_a/(4*7.83) = 15,066 km. I verified: 1.574*299792/(4*7.83) = 471872.6/31.32 = 15066.2 km — accurate. However the paragraph then says this is "66% higher than the dome's published H, destroying WIN-029's match to the firmament apex." The 66% figure uses H_dome=9086 km, but the SAME-CIRCUIT line on live-power.txt:147 explicitly uses H_0=8537 km. With H_0=8537: (15066-8537)/8537 = 76.5% — even worse for the dome. The paragraph picks the comparison favorable to the dome without flagging that the dome's own same-circuit framing uses the smaller H_0. Minor but a sharper version of the argument is available for free.

kernel_of_truth.description: Tesla's estimate of 0.08484 s for round-trip pulse propagation is a real engineering input from a real patent (data/wins.json:WIN-001 detail_evidence — Tesla's 1905 patent US787412 is correctly cited and linked). The inverse is genuinely close to a Schumann-band frequency, and the relationship between his velocity figure (471,240 km/s) and the spherical-waveguide phase velocity pi*c/2 (=470,912 km/s, ratio 1.0007) is a real correspondence — Tesla was within 0.07% of the correct globe-cavity phase velocity (raw-text/08-live-power.txt:23 publishes v_a=1.574c, which is pi/2 rounded). The dome correctly notices these numerical relationships exist.
kernel_of_truth.why_it_doesnt_save_claim: Noticing that two derivations land at the same number does not make the underlying mechanism a flat disc (data/wins.json:WIN-001 detail_evidence — the closing paragraph: "v_a was fit to absorb that residual, so f=v_a/(2*r_disc) and f=c/(2*disc_thickness) agree at 11.787 Hz by construction, not by independent physics"). The chain runs in the opposite direction from what the dome claims: take a globe-cavity phase velocity, dress it as an aetheric wave speed, then express it via globe-derived geometric constants (pi*R_earth) re-labeled as dome parameters (r_disc). The dome's own history page concedes the original chain was circular (data/wins.json:WIN-001 detail_evidence — "the model's evolution page explicitly states it voluntarily removed circular reasoning (Tesla f→T→f) from its WIN count in an earlier version"); the current chain avoids explicit f→T→f circularity but preserves the relabeling problem.

deeper_analysis:
The c5→c6 patch closed a cosmetic
bug; the c6→c7 drift is content, not cosmetic. The EXP-263 insertion (8bb84ca6) of the c-vs-v_a swap paragraph is the substantive change. It is well-constructed: arithmetic verifies to 0.1% (v_a/(4*7.83)=15066 km; c/(2*r_disc)=7.49 Hz; both reproduced by independent computation here), the dispersion-law defense preempt is empirically supported (zero grep hits across the dome raw-text corpus for dispersion/mode/eigenvalue language), and the r=0.999 same-circuit citation is correctly sourced to live-power.txt:147. The remaining vulnerabilities are minor: (a) the dispersion-absence claim is a moving target, (b) the missing critique of the degenerate r=0.999 "correlation" leaves a sharp finding unused, (c) the secondary-source citation concession introduces an asymmetric epistemic vulnerability, (d) the 66% figure could be sharpened to 77% by using the same-circuit's own H_0=8537 km. Verdict holds without qualification. recommended_action=minor_edit reflects these are belt-and-braces improvements, not structural fixes.

advocate_mode.best_defense: A fair-minded dome defender accepting the six methodological principles plays the following remaining card after the c-vs-v_a paragraph lands: "You argue applying v_a consistently to WIN-029 inflates the firmament match from 5.3% to 66% — but this assumes a single propagation velocity across the cavity, which Maxwell's equations in a dispersive medium do not require. Phase velocity and group velocity differ by mode, and our aetheric medium has frequency-dependent index n(omega). When omega is at Tesla's 11.78 Hz the phase velocity is 1.574c; when omega is at Schumann's 7.83 Hz the group velocity (governing cavity reflection) is approximately c. There is no internal contradiction — there is a dispersion law you have not asked us to publish." The defense gives the dome a way to keep both WINs while conceding the c-vs-v_a difference is the *signature* of dispersion rather than the *defect* of fitting.
advocate_mode.preemptive_recommendation: Address head-on rather than asserting absence. Convert the current "the dome publishes no dispersion relation" sentence into a constructive challenge: "If the dome's response is that this c-vs-v_a difference reflects a dispersion law (different modes, different phase velocities), the burden is to publish that law: an explicit n(omega) curve showing how the medium's index varies between 7.83 Hz and 11.78 Hz, with both v_a=1.574c and v_phase=c emerging as solutions of a single dispersion equation evaluated at those frequencies. Until then, the per-WIN speed selection is parameter-fitting, not dispersion." This converts an absence-claim (vulnerable to one-paragraph reactive insertion) into a specification-demand (which a one-paragraph insertion cannot satisfy — the dome would need an n(omega) curve consistent across all aetheric WINs, not just these two).
